correctness.rationale: The source characteristic function gives \(\phi_\lambda(2\pi/3)=\cosh(\pi\lambda/3)/\cosh(\pi\lambda)\). The triple-angle identity reduces this exactly to the reciprocal of \(4\cosh^2(\pi\lambda/3)-3\), and \(\cos(2\pi X/3)\) is exactly a two-valued function of divisibility by three. Strong consistency follows from the strong law and continuity of the inverse. The CLT variance is reconstructed from \(E[\cos^2(2\pi X/3)]=(1+\phi_\lambda(4\pi/3))/2\), and the inverse delta method yields the displayed closed form. Algebra then gives the exact ratio to the source's parity variance, whose derivative is negative after setting \(z=\cosh^2(\pi\lambda/3)>1\). The small-scale efficiencies follow from the source's Fisher information and explicit limits. The bundled checker independently reproduces all identities on a parameter grid.

value.rationale: The direct source explicitly identifies the poor efficiency of its only closed-form estimator and asks for more efficient closed-form characteristic-function alternatives. The new statistic keeps the same one-frequency, explicit-inversion simplicity but improves asymptotic variance uniformly by at least \(5/32\) relative to that benchmark and raises the small-scale MLE-relative efficiency from \(3/4\) to \(8/9\). The divisibility-by-three form also makes the estimator computationally trivial. This directly advances the source's stated estimation gap rather than selecting an arbitrary transform frequency.
